                    Finding Unknown Quantities in Quadrilaterals and Pentagons
problem:
Given the pentagon $ABCDE$ shown below, find the value of $x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14186732/assets/dc4407245e0639d9055d9518088a46b310f67e897337bd8963e5b1c42a86421f.png)
worked_solution:
A pentagon has $n=5$ sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon must be 

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={180}^{∘}\cdot (5-2) \\  & ={180}^{∘}\cdot 3 \\  & ={540}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding up the internal angles and solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C+m∠D+m∠E & ={540}^{∘} \\ {120}^{∘}+{110}^{∘}+2x+{90}^{∘}+x+{40}^{∘} & ={540}^{∘} \\ 2x+x+{40}^{∘}+{120}^{∘}+{110}^{∘}+{90}^{∘} & ={540}^{∘} \\ 3x+{360}^{∘} & ={540}^{∘} \\ 3x & ={180}^{∘} \\ x & ={60}^{∘}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
